items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: The rhythm section was Ernest Hill, Lawrence Lucie, guitar, Teddy Wilson and me.

ctx.x: Well, Chick had the house band, right?

Yeah, yeah, at the Savoy. Ella was with the band. That was a great band, Chick Webb's band at that time. Sandy Williams on trombone, Taft Jordan, Wayman Carver, Elmer Williams, tenor saxophone, Wayman Carver was playing flute. I think Pauley was in that band too for a while. But that was a great band. Chick and Ella, oh goodness, I worked opposite Chick's band up there while I was with Willie Bryant. We worked opposite Chick's band for a year, a year and a half. Benny Carter was in the band then with Willie…
Before we get too much into that, let me ask you one thing about Wilbur Sweetman.

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWEE: ...Cozy Cole, right. ... They had Walter Page on a lot of the bass and on the drums, Cozy Cole and let's see, Joe Jones -- I think they did most of the drumming.

ctx.x: Yeah, he was tremendous; he did so much for that.

See, he could do that -- he had enough power and know how. He was a very smart man, you know, and jumping forward a little bit, when the color line was broken with the staff radio musicians, you know, John Hammond called on the phone the President of the corporation and said to mix up the band and that he wanted a mixed band in the studio, so they did it. And the NAACP was having rallies in Madison Square Garden and marching up and down the street, and nothing was happening. Here John Hammond gets on the phone,…
